title: Seacliff Logistics inference integration scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Quick POC call with Seacliff Logistics (ops + infra + data) 2025-02-10. They move ~200k orders/day, need LLM for ETA summarization, exception detection, and chat assist for dispatchers.
- Stage: evaluating inference topology (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Primary constraints: EU residency for some customers, strict audit logs, max 75ms p99 latency for chat suggestions, cost target ~$0.0008 per generated token for bulk batch jobs.

Attendees:
- Seacliff: Maya Patel (Head of Digital Ops), Tomasz Kowalczyk (Platform), Aine Murphy (Data Science)
- Redwood: Marisa Chen (solutions), Ravi Singh (infra), Nora Watanabe (security)
notes:
Call notes / raw:
- Maya: use case is near-real-time suggestions for dispatchers (single-turn, short prompts ~30-80 tokens). Also nightly batch summarization of delay reasons across orders (longer sequences).
- Tomasz: infra preference = private deployment into Seacliff GCP project (they have strict VPC rules). Want a control plane in our cloud but data plane in their VPC or a dedicated private deployment.
- Aine: model quality matters for extraction of structured fields (cause_code, expected_delay_min). Will test a few open LLMs; prefers models with deterministic NER for downstream metrics.
- Security notes: must integrate with their corporate KMS (Cloud KMS), require HMAC-signed audit events forwarded to their SIEM, retention 2 years.
- SLA ask: p99 latencies under 75ms for chat; can tolerate eventual consistency for batch summarization jobs.
- Throughput: peak dispatcher concurrency ~120 active sessions, average QPS for chat ~40qps, spikes to 200qps in heavy hours. Nightly batch runs ~30k documents to summarize.
- Data: examples include long order history prefixes (prefix length sometimes >3k tokens) which will break naive sequence limits and cause high compute if not truncated/ cached.
- Integration: existing platform exposes Kafka topic for events + REST API for agent UI. Prefer webhooks for async results.

Technical requirements (draft):
- Deployment: private deployment with control plane in Redwood hosted; data plane either dedicated in Seacliff VPC or Redwood-managed dedicated nodes peered to Seacliff.
- Networking: VPC peering or Private Service Connect. Must support mutual TLS and token-based service account auth.
- Key mgmt: integrate Cloud KMS; support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and HSM-backed keys for production.
- Auditing: per-request audit log with request_id, model_version, prompt_hash, token_count, latency_ms forwarded to Seacliff SIEM (syslog/HTTPS).
- Model constraints: start with quantized 8-bit variants of open-weights (Vicuna/Redwood-curated). Fallback policy to smaller Llama2-7b when capacity constrained.
- Cost controls: suggest batching for nightly summaries, but keep dispatcher suggestions single-shot streaming enabled.

Gotchas & early-red-flags:
- Long prefix behavior: their order history can cause >2k token prefixes. Need prefix KV cache or early-truncation policies; risk of huge compute and cost.
- Kafka integration: they want exactly-once semantics for event->inference pipeline; we should confirm ordering guarantees and idempotency keys.
- Latency SLO: 75ms p99 is tight for token-generation if we do large context windows and quantized models on shared hardware. Consider dedicated low-latency instances and pre-warming.
- Data residency: EU customers must only see models hosted in eu-west-1; need routing policy per-customer.
- Monitoring: they require per-customer cost breakdown and token-level billing exports. Our defaults may need customization.

Prototype plan / timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (2025-02-17): access + onboarding: get Seacliff GCP project id, service account for VPC peering test, initial sample dataset (anonymized) + KMS test keys. Owner: Tomasz (Seacliff) + Marisa (Redwood).
- Week 1 (2025-02-24): deploy POC in their VPC (small footprint): basic REST endpoint, simple webhook callback, streaming chat for dispatchers. Owner: Ravi.
- Week 2 (2025-03-03): run perf tests (load gen up to 200qps), measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, tune batching and instance types. Deliver perf report. Owner: Ravi + Marisa.
- Week 3 (2025-03-10): run accuracy/QA with Aine: structured extraction tests, regressions, hallucination checks. Owner: Aine + Nora (security).
- Week 4 (2025-03-17): produce go/no-go for pilot + rough TCO. Owner: Marisa.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Is Seacliff willing to accept dedicated nodes (monthly commit) vs fully private on-prem license? If dedicated nodes, what's the expected monthly spend? (need commitment for capacity planning).
- For EU-only customers, do they want a per-customer routing policy or a tenant-level org setting? (affects complexity).
- How to handle long historical prefixes semantically? Truncate vs. summarization vs. selective context retrieval (we should propose retrieval + concise summary of last 5 events).
- Exact SIEM endpoint and format for audit logs (syslog, JSON over HTTPS). Need sample.

Immediate next steps (today):
- Marisa: send follow-up email with onboarding checklist + request for anonymized sample data (orders with typical length distributions). Due: 2025-02-11.
- Tomasz: share GCP project ID + test SA for peering. Due: 2025-02-14.
- Ravi: prepare a rough perf-run plan and instance recommendations (including low-latency instance types) by 2025-02-14.
- Nora: draft a compliance checklist mapping to their retention/KMS/SIEM asks by 2025-02-15.

Quick wins / workaround suggestions:
- For early POC, run dispatcher chat on a dedicated small pool with aggressive KV caching to hold recent order context and keep generation windows small (~256 tokens).
- Nightly summarization can batch 30k docs using optimized batching (max tokens/batch) and run on cheaper preemptible/dedicated instances to meet cost target.

Notes-to-self:
- Bring up retrieval augmentation idea: canonicalize last-5 events -> condensed 120-token summary appended to prompt. Low-risk for 75ms SLO.
- Check if we have an example SIEM JSON mapping for per-request audit logs (ask Nora).
- Add a quick demo script that shows token-level cost calc for 30k nightly docs vs streaming chat.

References / links to later attach:
- Example dataset (anonymized) link placeholder: seacliff-sample-orders.csv
- Related Redwood doc: private-deployments/networking-checklist (link to attach after upload)

Status: rough draft, capture of POC kickoff. Many items intentionally terse — expand into formal runbook once Seacliff confirms deployment model.
summary: Working scratchpad for Seacliff Logistics POC: call notes, constraints, technical requirements, gotchas, timeline and next steps. Focus on private deployment, KMS integration, SIEM auditing, latency SLOs, and handling long order prefixes.
